metadata.title: Systematic strategies for developing phage resistant Escherichia coli strains

reference.title: Systematic strategies for developing phage resistant Escherichia coli strains

target.condition: LB, 37 C, 100 ug/mL ampicillin; phage challenge at MOI 0.05/0.5/5 at OD600 0.6 (growth curves, 12 h) or t=0 per Fig. 1c caption; plaque spot assay 12 h; EOP overnight

trigger.observation: The SspABCD-SspE system was recently identified by the group as a PT-modulated defense system with broad antiphage activity and no toxicity to hosts lacking sspABCD, making it a candidate module for host protection (p005); plasmid delivery chosen as the quick evaluation route before genome integration.
trigger.reasoning: Validate that plasmid-borne SspBCDE from E. coli 3234/A confers DNA PT modification and broad phage protection in laboratory/industrial E. coli hosts without growth cost
trigger.source_location: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (primary); extended to MG1655(DE3), W3110, BW25113, JM109, E. coli B OP50, wild-type E. coli W

evidence.source_location: Same hosts with empty vector pBluescript II SK(+); LB blank reference

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Outcome measured directly by EOP, plaque assays and growth curves.

alternatives.approach: Plasmid-encoded natural antiphage systems previously used in dairy starter strains (CRISPR-Cas, Abi, antisense mRNA, R-M) noted as background approaches with narrow range or postsegregational killing risk
R-M systems rejected implicitly because REase loss causes host cell death; SspE chosen because it is non-toxic without sspABCD

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Transformation with pWHU3640 (pBluescript II SK(+) carrying ~8 kb sspBCDE cassette cloned from E. coli 3234/A genomic DNA via PCR + Gibson assembly)

result.metric: OD600 growth curves, plaque size/morphology, EOP fold protection
result.after: Up to 10^6-fold protection against most tested coliphages; no protection against T5; no growth impairment; protection observed across all 7 host backgrounds

decision_chain.rule: When engineering phage resistance into phage-sensitive E. coli production hosts, first evaluate the candidate defense module on a plasmid across multiple host backgrounds and a phage panel spanning all three Caudovirales morphological families, because module efficacy is host- and phage-dependent and plasmid delivery allows rapid screening before committing to genome integration.

target.condition: LB, 37 C; kanamycin 50 ug/mL selection; overnight 42 C curing

trigger.observation: Plasmid-encoded defense is limited by plasmid incompatibility, instability, copy-number variability and metabolic burden of plasmid maintenance (results_p002, citing refs 36, 37).
trigger.reasoning: Generate stable phage-resistant strain avoiding plasmid incompatibility, instability, copy-number variation and metabolic burden

evidence.source_location: MG1655 parent and MG1655(pWHU3640) for growth and expression comparison

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Integration verified by colony PCR and genome sequencing; protection gain measured by EOP.

alternatives.approach: Continued use of plasmid-borne sspBCDE (rejected due to plasmid incompatibility/instability/copy-number/metabolic burden)

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Integration of 5.4 kb sspBCD at safe site SS9 (int(aslA-glmZ)) via pKOV-Kan two-step double crossover (pWHU6401); subsequent lambda-red recombineering integration of 2.6 kb sspE with FRT-Kan marker (pKD46 induced with 0.2% arabinose; pKD13 template), marker excision with pCP20, plasmid curing at 42 C, verification by colony PCR and genome sequencing -> E. coli-PT strains

result.metric: Colony PCR, genome sequencing, growth profile, RT-qPCR sspE:sspBCD ratio, EOP
result.after: MG1655-PT grows like MG1655(pWHU3640); sspE:sspBCD ratio slightly higher; at least 10-fold increased protection against T1, T4, EEP, lambda vs plasmid system

decision_chain.rule: When converting a plasmid-borne defense or pathway module into a stable industrial E. coli host, integrate the module at a characterized intergenic safe site (e.g., SS9) using markerless two-step double-crossover plus lambda-red recombineering, because chromosomal integration removes plasmid-instability and antibiotic-selection burdens while preserving host viability.

target.condition: LB, 37 C; sequential construction; verification by genome sequencing

trigger.observation: EOP data showed phage T5 was insensitive to SspBCDE defense (results_p001) and T7 remained a threat; known biology: T1/T5/phi80 use FhuA as receptor (ref 41) and T7 uses host TrxA as processivity factor (ref 42).
trigger.reasoning: Achieve tolerance to phages T5 and T7, which evaded or were insufficiently restricted by SspBCDE alone

evidence.source_location: WT, plasmid-bearing and -PT counterparts in each background

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Insensitivity of T5 measured by EOP (hard data); receptor/factor roles grounded in cited experimental literature; outcome verified by plaque/EOP/growth assays.
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Deletion of FhuA extracellular loop 8 (fhuA Delta552-558 with NESG peptide insertion to preserve beta-barrel formation) via pWHU6402 two-step double crossover, followed by trxA deletion via pWHU6403 -> E. coli-EPR strains

result.metric: Plaque assay, EOP, growth curves at MOI up to 10, phage cocktail challenge
result.after: Plaques barely formed on EPR lawns even at highest phage titer; no lysis by T1/T5/EEP/JMPW2 at MOI 10; significant resistance to T4/T7 at MOI 0.1 and lambda at MOI 0.5; identical growth to parents; resistant to 7-phage cocktail

decision_chain.rule: When a DNA-level defense system leaves specific phages unrestricted in an E. coli production host, layer receptor/essential-host-factor mutations targeting those phages' infection cycle (e.g., delete FhuA loop 8 for FhuA-dependent phages, delete trxA for T7-family polymerase dependence) on top of the defense module, because phages unable to inject or replicate DNA cannot escape through restriction-insensitivity mechanisms.
